rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose noun for an amount or intake that is more than needed, especially food, drink, or medicine.

example.english: Taking this medicine to excess can hurt your stomach.
example.traditional: 呢隻藥食到過量會傷胃。
example.jyutping: ni1 zek3 joek6 sik6 dou3 gwo3 loeng6 wui5 soeng1 wai6

rows.note: Use this when the excess is measured against a stated limit, quota, or permitted amount.

example.english: Our electricity use was in excess of the quota this month, so we have to pay a surcharge.
example.traditional: 今個月用電超額，要交附加費。
example.jyutping: gam1 go3 jyut6 jung6 din6 ciu1 ngaak6 jiu3 gaau1 fu6 gaa1 fai3

rows.note: Use this for the remainder or balance left after one amount is subtracted from another, rather than for excess in general.

example.english: The excess in the account after rent was deducted was three thousand dollars.
example.traditional: 扣咗房租之後，戶口仲有三千蚊餘額。
example.jyutping: kau3 zo2 fong4 zou1 zi1 hau6 wu6 hau2 zung6 jau5 saam1 cin1 man1 jyu4 ngaak6

rows.note: Use this specifically for the act of overindulging by eating and drinking too much.

example.english: Over Chinese New Year, I kept eating and drinking to excess, and my stomach couldn't take it.
example.traditional: 過年成日暴飲暴食，個肚頂唔順。
example.jyutping: gwo3 nin4 seng4 jat6 bou6 jam2 bou6 sik6 go3 tou5 ding2 m4 seon6
